Day 37 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

Ansible Loops

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished after ledger snapshot

Loops reduce repetitive tasks while keeping each item visible in Ansible's result model.

Architecture / mental model

task + iterable items → one module invocation per item → per-item results

How it works

Loops are useful for repetitive resources such as users, directories or small sets of configuration entries.

They should not replace a module's native ability to accept a list when batching is clearer or more efficient. Package modules, for example, can often receive a list of packages in one task.

Registered loop results are nested per item, so later logic must understand the result structure instead of assuming it looks like a single task result.

Hands-on reference

# loop:
#   - alice
#   - bob
# ansible.builtin.user:
#   name: '{{ item }}'
#   state: present

Verification

Inspect `changed` and failed state per item and rerun to confirm the loop converges rather than recreating work.

Field note / gotcha

Looping a package-install task one package at a time can be an unnecessary anti-pattern when the module accepts the complete package list directly.

Security considerations

When items come from external data, validate them before using them in paths, shell commands or privileged resource names.

What I learned

A loop should make intent shorter without making result handling harder to understand.
